problem.title: The Problem
problem.scenario_increase: Starting in April 2026, your Philadelphia tax bill will increase by:
problem.impact_examples: That's between 1 and 3 months' rent for many Philadelphians who simply can't afford it.
problem.stat_desc: That includes 75,000 Philadelphians who own and operate single-owner entities: contractors, freelancers, gig workers, nurses, barbers, food truck vendors, artists, retailers, and more.
problem.intro: For 10 years, Philadelphia's smallest businesses had a shield from BIRT (Business Income and Receipts Tax)—letting them start, grow, and support their families. In 2026, that shield is gone.

solution.title: The Solution: The LIFT Act
solution.intro2: This class includes Laborers (Independent Contractors), and any individual or family enterprises with an individual owner (including those with employees).
solution.legal_note: Meets PA Constitution's Uniformity Clause requirements. Confirmed by Philadelphia Law Dept.

enables.title: What the LIFT Act Enables
enables.item1: ✓ City Council and the Mayor can legally remove BIRT for the LIFT class* completely
enables.item2: ✓ NPT tax remains, ensuring fair taxation instead of the current double-taxation structure
enables.item3: ✓ Keeps money in local neighborhoods—every dollar retained turns into $3+ in local spending

solution.intro: Pioneering legislation introduced in November 2025 by Councilman Mike Driscoll, the LIFT Act fixes the system instead of patching it by acknowledging a tax class that already exists but is unrecognized by current BIRT law.
solution.result: Result for an individual or family earning $50K: completely eliminates the surprise tax increase
solution.footnote:
*LIFT class includes Laborers (Independent Contractors), and any individual or family enterprises
with an individual owner (including those with employees).

action1.title: Calculate Your Increase Before Filing
action1.body: Use the calculator at liftphilly.org/calculator to see your tax increase, then share it with your professional network so they can calculate theirs.

action2.title: Start Conversations
action2.quote: "If you had to pay 1-3 months extra rent in taxes in 2026 and beyond, how would that affect your ability to care for yourself, your family, and your community?"
action2.follow: Then listen. Report back what you hear.

action3.title: Help Us Reach the Whole City
action3.p1: Share this information with your friends & trusted community leaders, and help us grow our network of networks.
action3.p2: Know someone who can help spread the word through your community, share their experiences as an individual business owner, or both? We're looking for both formal leaders and informal connectors.

action4.title: Identify Testimony Voices
action4.intro: We're building a coalition that reflects all of Philadelphia—every zip code, every background, every identity. Help us find powerful voices from:

This resource is not intended to be legal advice and your legal and tax advisors should be consulted.
The LIFT class does not include S-Corp and C-Corp entities.

principles.solution_focused: Solution-focused, not political. We're all Philadelphians solving a problem together.
principles.no_blame: The problem is in the system, not individuals. No blame, no shame. The system was designed for a different economy.
principles.shepherd: Shepherd mindset. Shepherds focus on solutions with love. Be the shepherd when advocating for LIFT. In the room with us? Share your fear, uncertainty, and doubt—we'll help you through it.
